title: Identify the major categories of ornamental plants

lessons.title: Trees, shrubs and climbers
lessons.html:
Trees, shrubs and climbers

In a nursery or garden there are many kinds of plants. We sort them into groups, called categories. When you know the groups, you know how big a plant will grow and how to look after it.

Trees

A tree is a big woody plant with one main stem, called a trunk. It grows tall, often more than 4 metres. Examples: wild olive, white stinkwood, cabbage tree (kiepersol), coral tree, jacaranda.

  • Trees give shade.
  • Do not plant big trees too close to houses, walls or pipes. The roots can break them.

Shrubs

A shrub is a woody plant with many stems from the ground. It is smaller than a tree. Examples: plumbago, wild dagga, buddleja, hydrangea, rosemary, roses.

  • Shrubs are used for hedges, screens and flower beds.
  • Many are pruned to keep a nice shape.

Climbers

A climber has long, weak stems. It needs a wall, fence or frame to hold it up. Examples: bougainvillea, star jasmine, Cape honeysuckle, golden shower.

  • Some climbers have thorns, like bougainvillea. Wear gloves.
  • Tie them to a frame while they are young.

Evergreen and deciduous

An evergreen plant keeps its leaves all year. A deciduous plant drops its leaves in autumn or winter and grows new ones in spring. A jacaranda is deciduous for a short time. A wild olive is evergreen.

When you plant or sell a plant, read the label. It tells you the plant name, the category, how big it grows, and if it likes sun or shade. If a label is lost, ask your team leader before you guess.

lessons.title: Flowers, groundcovers, grasses and succulents
lessons.html:
Flowers, groundcovers, grasses and succulents

Annuals

An annual lives for one season. It grows, flowers, makes seed and dies in less than a year. Examples: petunia, marigold, alyssum, pansy, Namaqualand daisy. Annuals give lots of colour. They are planted again each season.

Perennials

A perennial lives for more than two years. It is usually soft, not woody. Examples: agapanthus, wild iris (dietes), clivia, daylily. Perennials come back every year.

Bulbs

A bulb plant stores food under the ground in a bulb, corm or tuber. It rests part of the year. Examples: gladiolus, nerine, freesia, amaryllis. Many beautiful bulbs come from South Africa.

Groundcovers

Groundcovers are low plants that spread over the soil. They cover bare ground and stop weeds and soil washing away. Examples: vygies, ivy geranium, gazania.

Grasses

Lawn grasses are cut short to make a lawn: kikuyu, buffalo grass, Cynodon (kweek). Ornamental grasses grow tall for decoration.

Succulents

Succulents have thick leaves or stems that store water. They need little water. Examples: aloes, crassula (pig's ear, jade plant), vygies. Many are indigenous. They are good in waterwise gardens.

CategoryExample
TreeWild olive
ShrubPlumbago
ClimberBougainvillea
AnnualPetunia
PerennialAgapanthus
BulbGladiolus
SucculentAloe

Some plants are poisonous, for example the sap of some euphorbias and the oleander shrub. Wear gloves and wash your hands. Never eat any part of a garden plant.

Key points

  • Trees have one trunk; shrubs have many woody stems.
  • Climbers need support.
  • Annuals live one season; perennials come back every year.
  • Succulents store water and need little watering.
  • Some plants are poisonous; wear gloves and wash your hands.
